{"model_version":"litellm_proxy/openai/gpt-6-luna","content":{"parts":[{"text":"An **agent trace** is a record of what an AI agent did while handling a task, usually arranged as a time-ordered sequence or a tree of related steps. There is no single universal format: in observability tools, it usually means an execution record; in research, it can mean the agent’s action trajectory.

Typical trace components include:

- **The task and result:** the request received and the agent’s final response.
- **Steps taken:** model calls, tool calls and results, and handoffs between agents.
- **Timing and diagnostics:** timestamps, duration, errors, and sometimes token use or cost.
- **Context and metadata:** identifiers, configuration, or state needed to interpret the run.

**Purpose:** traces help people debug failures, understand behavior, evaluate performance, and monitor cost or reliability. A trace may include prompts or other sensitive data, so what gets recorded depends on the system and its privacy settings.

A trace does **not** necessarily contain the model’s private reasoning or “chain of thought.” It is better understood as a record of observable execution steps, unless a particular system defines it differently.

**Grounding:** OpenTelemetry describes traces as connected spans that represent work across a system, and its GenAI conventions cover AI-related operations. The OpenAI Agents SDK documents traces of agent runs, model calls, tool calls, and handoffs.

- [OpenTelemetry: Traces](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/signals/traces/)
- [OpenTelemetry: GenAI semantic conventions](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/)
